correctness.rationale: The excluded supports are the empty set and the size-at-least-two subsets of each individual part, disjointly. On an entire part the character sum is 2^n_i for a zero block and zero otherwise, while the singleton sum is n_i−2w_i. Subtraction gives the stated unnormalized eigenvalues and the strictly positive trivial eigenvalue d. The feasible all-blocks-nonzero weights are all integers from t through N. They include (N+t)/2 for eigenvalue −1 in the even N−t case, and (N+t−1)/2 and (N+t+1)/2 for eigenvalues 0 and −2 in the odd case (N≥t+1). Parity gives the matching lower bounds and the triangle inequality gives maximum d. Generating polynomials enumerate the disjoint proper-zero-block classes. In the singular case their aggregate differs from the central weight layer by at most twice the number of frequencies missing some part; the union bound and central binomial estimate give the stated limit. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 5 used graph searches on induced vertex subsets, direct signed sums and multiplicities of block-weight vectors on seven profiles (through N=8); for K_{2,3} and K_{2,2,2} it gave nullities 12 and 24. This computation corroborates the finite examples, not the infinite theorem or asymptotic.
